top_choice_rationale: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a compact prediction-then-discovery chain: the 2011 flat-band prediction by Bistritzer and MacDonald and the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states by the Jarillo-Herrero group. The phenomenology has been reproduced by independent groups and fabrication routes, with twist angle, gating and pressure as a clean control knob, so the prize would recognise a reproduced observation and not an explanation. The costs are real: eight years of maturity, an unresolved pairing mechanism, and an omitted first author (Cao) and parallel groups, which the citation wording crediting the Jarillo-Herrero group only partly softens. I still judge it the larger scientific step than optical lattice clocks (P001), which I rank second as a mature, cleanly attributed Katori and Ye award that I read as extending the line honoured in 2005 and 2012. No award (P000) is last because a defensible, reproduced achievement is available.
